# Bona fide community name terms

These terms apply to every name on the .simplex list of bona fide community
names. You accept them when you register or receive such a name, and they bind
everyone who holds it after you.

## What a bona fide name is for

A bona fide community name speaks for a community: a place, a language, a
profession, a cause, a project, or any other group of people the name points
to. Whoever holds it must use it in good faith, for the benefit of that
community. The holder must not:

- use the name for purposes unrelated to the community it names;
- use it to mislead the community, to impersonate anyone, or to speak for the
  community against its will;
- keep it idle, or hold it mainly to resell it or to keep others from serving
  the community.

## A lease for the registered term

Registering or receiving a bona fide name gives you its use until it expires,
and nothing beyond that. The fee pays for that term only. Renewal is not a
right: the consortium that operates the .simplex namespace (the Consortium)
allows it only to holders who have used the name in line with these terms.

## Renewal and reassignment

Before a name expires, the Consortium may ask its holder to show how the name
serves its community, for example through what it is used for or through the
support of the community's members. If the Consortium finds that the name is
not used in line with these terms, it may block its renewal. Once the term and
the grace period after it have ended, the Consortium may assign the name to
another party it considers better placed to serve the community.

The Consortium decides in good faith and may hear the community first. It does
not take a name away or change its records during a term the holder has paid
for, and fees already paid are not refunded.

## Transfers

A transfer passes on the remaining term, not more. The recipient must accept
these terms before receiving the name.

## Changes

The Consortium may publish new terms. They apply to registrations and
transfers made under them, and a holder may be asked to accept the current
terms in order to renew.
